title: The awaited Imam
hookLine: Twelver Shia hold that the twelfth Imam, al-Mahdi, is in occultation and will return

cards: In some homes, when a certain name is spoken, people stand, or put a hand on their heart, and say a short phrase asking God to hasten his coming. The name is the Mahdi, the rightly guided one.
For Twelver Shia Muslims he is not a figure from a book of prophecies only. He is a person, the twelfth Imam, the son of the eleventh, alive and hidden, and they await his return. The awaited Imam.

teach.h: THE SON OF THE ELEVENTH IMAM.
teach.b: Twelver Shia teaching says this. The eleventh Imam, Hasan al-Askari, had a son, Muhammad.
When his father died, the boy was withdrawn from the world by God's will, into what is called the ghaybah, the occultation, the hiddenness.

For a time, a few trusted deputies carried his word to the believers; this is called the lesser occultation. Then the last deputy died, and the greater occultation began, which Twelvers hold continues today.

The Imam is alive, they say, aware of the world, unseen, and at a time only God knows he will appear, and Jesus will return with him, and together they will set the world right. The word that keeps coming back is justice.

teach.h: HE WILL FILL THE EARTH WITH JUSTICE.
teach.b: A hadith in the collection of Abu Dawud says that even if only a single day of the world remained, God would lengthen it until He sent a man from the Prophet's family, peace be upon him, who would fill the earth with fairness and justice as it had been filled with oppression.
Sunni Muslims know that hadith too.
In Sunni teaching that accepts these reports, the Mahdi is someone still to come, not the hidden twelfth Imam.
So both hope, in different shapes. For Twelvers the hope is very near: an Imam already here, waiting, and believers who try to live as though he might arrive tomorrow.
A week that began with a river cut off, after so much injustice, closes on a waiting.

how: Twelver Shia Muslims hold that the twelfth Imam is alive in occultation; they ask God to hasten his reappearance, and the fifteenth of Sha'ban, remembered as his birthday, is a night of celebration.

o: the hiddenness: the twelfth Imam, alive and unseen
the last day, when the dead are raised to life

games.q: the awaited Imam — tap the pairs.
p: he will fill the earth with justice

s: only Shia Muslims speak of a Mahdi
Sunni collections such as Abu Dawud's carry Mahdi reports too; Sunni teaching sees him as still to come.
Twelvers hold the twelfth Imam is alive now, unseen
they say he is in the greater occultation and will return.
the Mahdi in these teachings comes to punish one group of people
the word that keeps coming back is justice: filling the earth with it.

games.q: you believe a just leader could appear at any moment. how do you live today?
o: wait passively; it's out of your hands.
try to live as though he might arrive tomorrow.
stop caring about injustice until he comes.
games.why: Twelver teaching links the waiting to living rightly now, as though the Imam might come tomorrow.

practice: Bring to mind one injustice you know about, in the news or on your own street, and neither solve it nor look away from it. Let yourself want it to be set right.
Then hold one quiet question gently: if justice were arriving tomorrow, what would I want to have done today?

wordCard.voice: Ghaybah, the hiddenness: for Twelver Shia Muslims, the state of the twelfth Imam, al-Mahdi, alive and unseen, coming back to fill the earth with justice. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: absence or hiddenness; for Twelvers, the occultation of the twelfth Imam.

carryVoice: Your line: awaiting justice. Waiting, here, is not idle. Day eight hundred ninety-six, and a week complete.
